summary: Concierge Overlay URL-routing verification — ALL OVERLAY BEHAVIOURS PASSED on /about. Verified via Playwright: (1) SiteHeader with 'Meet George or Georgia' button visible on /about, (2) clicking it opens overlay with correct heading, welcome text, and both CTAs, (3) /about content remains in DOM behind blurred backdrop (URL unchanged), (4) 'I'll explore myself' fades overlay away leaving user on /about, (5) ESC key closes overlay, (6) 'Show me around' navigates to /meet?from=concierge. Curl confirmed the routing situation: localhost:3001/about → 200 Next.js (marketing, contains 'Meet George or Georgia' text), localhost:3000/ → 200 Expo mobile-app HTML (title 'FriendPlace', expo-reset styles, no SiteHeader). /admin/knowledge spot-check returned 200. No code changes required.
action_items: Direct Garry to any Next.js-routed marketing path (/about, /how-it-works, /features, /meet, etc.) to demo the concierge overlay in this preview environment. The bare / URL is nginx-routed to the Expo mobile app (port 3000) and always will be in this preview; production (friendplace.com.au) will have the marketing site on its own domain with no such conflict.

MINOR OBSERVATION (not tested-blocking): The review request states 'The countdown ribbon should still be visible at the top of the /about page (since it's in the same layout).' However, code inspection shows LaunchCountdownRibbon is rendered ONLY inside /app/website/app/page.tsx (the homepage), NOT in the root layout.tsx. Therefore the ribbon does not, and is not expected to, appear on /about. If Garry expects the ribbon on every marketing page, main agent should move <LaunchCountdownRibbon /> into layout.tsx (fetching launch status via a server component wrapper). If ribbon is intentionally home-only, no change needed — just correct the docstring in layout.tsx which currently says '+ adds ribbon' (it does not).
critical_code_review_comments: ConciergeOverlay: focus trap, ESC handler, body scroll lock, restore-focus-on-close, backdrop-click-closes and reduced-motion opt-out are all correctly implemented. Component is portable, single-file, and correctly a client component. No issues.
SiteHeader.openConcierge correctly preserves modifier-key opens (Cmd/Ctrl/Shift/Alt/middle-click still navigate to /meet as a JS-off fallback). Good accessibility.
layout.tsx comment on line 85–87 says the overlay '+ adds ribbon' — misleading, layout does NOT add ribbon. Small doc fix.
context_for_next_testing_agent: ConciergeOverlay verified working end-to-end on /about at the preview URL. Overlay triggers via CustomEvent 'friendplace:meet-george'. Any Next.js-routed marketing page will host it via the root layout. The bare '/' path is intentionally nginx-routed to the Expo mobile app and is NOT the correct URL to test the overlay in this preview environment.
rca_of_issue: Original bug: Garry visited https://george-mcgs-cms.preview.emergentagent.com/ expecting the marketing homepage. Nginx ingress (/app/config/nginx/*.conf) routes / → port 3000 (Expo mobile app) and only specific paths (/about, /how-it-works, /features, /faqs, /meet, /register-interest, /success-stories, /list-your-event, /contact, /privacy, /terms, /butterfly-lab, /admin/*) → port 3001 (Next.js marketing). This is intentional preview-only routing. In production the marketing site is on friendplace.com.au (its own domain) and the conflict disappears. No code change required; only user guidance about which URL to visit until production launch.
